court: In the High Court of Madras
respondents: Secretary to Government, Home Department, Fort St. George and Others … Respondent(s).
sections_referred: Tamil Nadu Liquor retail Vending (in Shops and Bars) Rules, 2003
advocates: For Respondent(s): Mr. C. Prabakaran, Govt. Counsel for R 1,2, 4 & 5
Mr. Balakrishnan, Standing Counsel for R 3
judgment_text:
Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of Constitution of India, to issue a writ of mandamus, directing the respondents to close and move the TASMAC wine shop No. 4015 and bar situated at Thimmarajakulam, chengalpattu District to any other authorised place by considering the representations dated 24-7-2024, 16-8-2024 and 10-3-2026.

The Order of the Court was delivered by

M. Dhandapani, J.:— The writ petition has been filed seeking a direction toa the respondents to close and move the TASMAC wine shop No. 4015 and bar situated at Thimmarajakulam, chengalpattu District to any other authorised place by considering the representations dated 24-7-2024, 16-8-2024 and 10-3-2026.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that the petitioner is residing in the Thimmarajakulam vicinity for the past four decades. Thimmarajakulam road is narrow road and the said is the only access available to the residents for their day-to-day activities. The Tasmac shop vide shop No. 4015 managed by the 3rd respondent herein is situated in thea bove said residential area. The shop functions 24 × 7, leading to gathering of drunkards, public nuisance, and safety issues. Women and Children are facing immense difficulty moving on the road in broad daylight due to fright and harassment. Therefore, the petitioner made a representations dated 24-7-2024, 16-8-2024 and 10-3-2026 and mp reply or action was taken by the respondents. Due to inaction by the authorities despite repeated complaints, and continued nuisance affecting residential tranquillity, petitioner has approached this Court.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the Thimmarajakulam road is heavily depended by the residents of the said area and the said TASMAC wine shop is operated in such residential area by the third respondent. The said wine shop along with bar is causing disturbance and affecting the peaceful life of the residents of Thimmarajakulam.

4. The learned counsel further submitted that as per Rule 8(1) of Tamil Nadu Liquor retail Vending Rules, 2003 which prohibits liquor shops within 100 meters of places of worship and educational institutions. Also violates Rule 9 - prescribed hours are 12 noon to 10 p.m. only.

5. Heard both sides and perused the materials available on record.

6. On perusal of the same, this Court finds that running a Tasmac shop 24 × 7 in a residential area, in proximity to temples, churches and a college, requires immediate examination. Hence, this Court passes the following orders:

i. The second and third respondents are directed to conduct a joint inspection of TASMAC shop No. 4015, Thimmarajakulam Road, Chengalpattu, within a period of one week from the date of receipt of a copy of this order; to verify

a. Whether the shop is situated within 100 meters from any place of worship or educational institution as per Rule 8(1) of the Tamil Nadu Liquor retail Vending Rules, 2003;

b. Whether the shop is functioning in a residential area contrary to the Master Plan/Zoning Regulations;

c. Whether the shop is operating beyond the permissible hours of 12.00 noon to 10.00 p.m. as per Rule 9.

ii. If the shop is found to be in violation of Rule 8(1) or is functioning in a residential area without valid permission, the second and third respondents shall take immediate steps to shift/close the said TASMAC shop No. 4015, in accordance with law, within a period of one week, thereafter.

iii. In the interregnum, the second respondent shall ensure that TASMAC shop No. 4015 strictly adheres to the prescribed business hours of 12.00 noon to 10.00 p.m. and that no liquor is sold outside the said hours. The 4th and 5th respondents shall ensure adequate police patrolling to prevent nuisance by drunkards in the said locality.”

7. With the above directions, the writ petition stands disposed of. No costs. The respondents 2 & 3 shall file a status report, separately, before this Court on 18-6-2026 without fail. No costs.
